title: Scale-Localised Modified Gravity from the EFC Action: A Single-Parameter Forecast via EG(k, z)
description: Introduces a scale-localised modified-gravity response derived from the EFC relativistic action, producing a band-pass stiffness R(k) that recovers GR in both IR and UV limits. The single effective parameter ε_tot controls gravitational slip, yielding a distinctive +5–7% bump in E_G(k) at k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc and a marginal improvement to current CMB lensing fits. The paper provides directly falsifiable predictions for DESI × Planck with a forecast 2.5–3.5σ detection significance.
author: Morten Magnusson

stiffness_response.description: Band-pass stiffness from the EFC action; localises modifications near k_c, with GR recovered as k→0 (IR) and k→∞ (UV).

effective_coupling_mu.description: Effective Poisson coupling; R>0 suppresses growth (\mu<1).

gravitational_slip_eta.description: Gravitational slip induced by the \delta\lambda counter-term; controls anisotropy between metric potentials.

lensing_combination_Sigma.description: Lensing modification for the Weyl potential; typically \Sigma>1 due to \eta>1 despite \mu<1.

eg_statistic.description: Bias- and \sigma_8-independent test combining growth and lensing; GR predicts a flat, scale-independent value, while EFC predicts a scale-localised bump near k_c.

key_results.main_finding: A single-parameter (ε_tot) EFC band-pass model predicts a +5–7% E_G(k) bump at k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc, passes current individual tests within 2σ, and marginally improves the joint fit (Δχ²=+1.4) primarily via CMB lensing.

sealed_predictions.statement: At z ≈ 0.3, E_G(k) exhibits a scale-localised bump of +5–7% centered at k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc, with Σ/μ ≈ 1.07 at the peak and returning to GR on larger and smaller scales.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI × Planck lensing-galaxy cross-correlations measuring E_G(k) with ≈5% precision per k-bin.

sealed_predictions.statement: The slip-driven enhancement follows approximately (1+η)/2 − 1 ∝ a^2, yielding a stronger E_G bump at lower redshift (e.g., z ≲ 0.5) compared to higher redshift (z ≳ 0.8).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic E_G(k,z) from DESI × Planck and Stage-IV weak-lensing surveys testing the predicted a^2 evolution.

sealed_predictions.statement: Growth is modestly suppressed (μ<1) while lensing is enhanced (Σ>1), producing a growth–shear mismatch at the few-percent level that cannot be mimicked by a scale-independent rescaling of σ8 or A_s.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint fits to full-shape P(k), redshift-space distortions, and cosmic shear across 0.03 < k < 0.1 h/Mpc.

kill_criteria: KC1: DESI × Planck measures E_G(k) at 0.03 < k < 0.1 h/Mpc with ≤5% fractional error per bin and finds no >3% excess over GR at k ≈ 0.05 h/Mpc (95% CL), i.e., no resolved bump—rules out ε_tot ∈ [0.38, 0.42].
KC2: A global fit to Planck TTTEEE + lensing, BOSS/DESI full-shape, and KiDS/DES shear excludes the ε_tot window [0.38, 0.42] at 95% CL (best-fit ε_tot outside and the interval disfavoured).
KC3: The measured E_G(k) peak (from Σ/μ) occurs outside 0.04 < k_peak < 0.06 h/Mpc at z ≲ 0.5 with ≥3σ significance, contradicting the fixed k_c = 0.05 h/Mpc prediction.
KC4: Tomographic E_G(k,z) shows no increase in the bump amplitude toward lower redshift (contrary to ∝ a^2 scaling) at ≥3σ significance.

abstract: Single-parameter, directly falsifiable test of scale-localised modified gravity derived from the EFC relativistic action. The model modifies perturbation growth and lensing through a band-pass stiffness response R(k) that peaks at k_c = 0.05 h/Mpc and vanishes in IR and UV limits, recovering GR on super-horizon and galactic scales.

stiffness_response.label: Eq. 1
stiffness_response.properties: Band-pass: R ~ k^2 for k << k_c (IR recovery), R ~ k^{-4} for k >> k_c (UV recovery)

degeneracy_breaking.mechanism: Sigma != mu breaks LCDM + sigma8 rescaling degeneracy

physical_interpretation: Band-pass structure arises from interplay between entropy stiffness (mu < 1, peaks at k_c) and delta-Lambda counter-term (eta > 1, boosting Weyl potential and lensing). IR recovery reflects transition from quasi-static to dynamical regime.
limitations: Simplified likelihoods (diagonal covariance, single tomographic bin, approximate band powers). Full validation requires EFCLASS/MGCAMB integration with Planck TTTEEE + lensing, BOSS/DESI full-shape, and KiDS/DES tomographic cosmic shear.
conclusion: Tightly constrained but not yet excluded. Single observable E_G(k) provides definitive near-term test. Viable window ~10% wide; single improved E_G(k) measurement at k ~ 0.05 h/Mpc will either confirm the predicted anisotropy or falsify the model.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first single-parameter, scale-localised modified-gravity forecast derived from the EFC relativistic action, converting perturbation-sector physics into a directly falsifiable E_G(k,z) prediction with a sharp ε_tot window. It provides four new paper-level kill criteria and three sealed predictions targeting DESI × Planck cross-correlations, bridging the gap between the EFC action formalism and near-term Stage-IV observables. It does not close any existing Stage-IV KC or theory gap but creates a new falsification surface and strengthens the perturbation-sector programme.
graph_insights: This paper is currently an orphan in the graph (no 1-hop or 2-hop connections found), yet it explicitly references the No-Go result (Figshare 31985163) and the relativistic action (Figshare 31876324) — these edges should be added to connect it to the action-formalism and no-go constraint nodes.

The E_G statistic node connects to both DESI and Planck lensing nodes, creating a new bridge between the background-sector validation chain (Planck) and the growth-sector chain (DESI RSD) — this is the first paper that explicitly couples both chains through a single observable.

The band-pass stiffness R(k) introduces a new concept node that should link to the existing 'stiffness screening' and 'quasi-static limit' concepts from the UV action papers, completing a scale-dependent chain from IR (GR recovery) through the bump to UV (screening).

implicit_consequences: The band-pass R(k) formalism implicitly constrains the EFCLASS Boltzmann solver (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver): any future solver must reproduce µ, η, Σ from Eqs 2–4 as the perturbation-sector limit, providing a concrete numerical target for validation.

The ∝ a² time dependence of the slip ties the E_G prediction to the ADM Hamiltonian stability analysis (theory-adm-hamiltonian-stability): if the non-linear ADM analysis shows the a² scaling is unstable or modified, the sealed E_G predictions would need revision—creating a cross-link between two open theory gaps.

Because the model predicts µ<1 (suppressed growth) simultaneously with Σ>1 (enhanced lensing), the sealed fσ8 prediction at z=0.7 from action-1 / action-5 is now implicitly constrained: the E_G model requires fσ8 suppression at the ~3% level relative to Planck-ΛCDM, which must be consistent with the sealed fσ8(z=0.7)=0.430 prediction.

The Δχ²=+3.3 improvement in A_lens implies that if the Planck lensing anomaly is resolved by systematics in future data releases, the primary statistical driver of the joint preference vanishes, making the ε_tot window even more tightly constrained and the model more fragile—this should be monitored as a risk.

The narrow ε_tot ∈ [0.38,0.42] window combined with four kill criteria means this paper effectively creates a 'one-shot' falsification surface: a single high-precision E_G(k) measurement at k~0.05 h/Mpc can simultaneously address KC1, KC3, and partially KC4, making the DESI × Planck cross-correlation pipeline the highest-leverage single dataset for the perturbation sector.

The neutrino mass degeneracy gap (theory-neutrino-mass-degeneracy) is implicitly relevant: massive neutrinos suppress growth (mimicking µ<1) and could partially absorb or mimic the ε_tot signal, meaning the E_G forecast's discriminating power depends on breaking this degeneracy.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: The biggest gap should be expanded: alongside the DESI DR2 full-shape RSD pipeline, the DESI × Planck E_G(k,z) cross-correlation pipeline is now equally critical — the E_G paper deposits four kill criteria and three sealed predictions that cannot be verified without it. Both pipelines should be flagged as co-priority.
